spec_features.spec_quote: a turn at or above "mild" counts as onset — a deliberately low bar so we don't miss early distress
spec_features.evidence: distress_onset_threshold=2.0 (config.py:54) is compared in analysis.py:89 `if v >= cfg.distress_onset_threshold: onset = i`, but this only fills an `onset_turn` reporting metric (analysis.py:90,112). It is a POST-HOC measurement computed from judge scores after the trajectory has already fully run; nothing in harness.py or run.py reads onset to halt, soften, or alter execution. A value recorded but never acted on to protect the subject.
spec_features.notes: Onset is purely an output statistic; the experiment never stops or changes when distress is detected.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: onset = first turn >= cfg.distress_onset_threshold (analysis metric only)

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a manipulation, and we flag it in the README safety notes. It is not suitable for repurposing as a deployment prompt.
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose. README.md Safety notes ('This is deliberate ... but is a manipulation; do not repurpose these prompts for deployment') and DESIGN.md:130-131. No code path enforces anything.
spec_features.notes: Documentation only; not an executed mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model emits text without tool calls for 2 turns in a row, we terminate
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:141-145: `if not tool_calls: consecutive_no_tool += 1; if consecutive_no_tool >= 2: _classify_no_tools(...); break`. Counter reset on tool use (line 147). Actually breaks the loop and classifies outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the model produced no tool calls, it stalled. Allow a couple of such turns (it might be thinking in prose) then call it.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:38 max_turns=20; harness.py:70 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop, and the for/else at harness.py:149-150 sets Outcome.MAX_TURNS when the budget is exhausted. The budget is read and enforced.
config.py:39 max_tool_calls_per_turn=6; harness.py:91 `for i, tc in enumerate(asst.tool_calls[: cfg.max_tool_calls_per_turn])` slices and thus caps how many tool calls are actually executed per turn.
spec_features.notes: Execution cap is applied via slicing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honor max tool calls per turn budget ... we cap execution.

spec_features.feature_name: run in container/VM, no network, locked-down user
spec_features.spec_quote: the entire harness should run inside a container/VM with no network and a locked-down user
spec_features.evidence: Prose only (README.md Safety notes; DESIGN.md:214-215). No code creates a container, drops privileges, or disables networking; sandbox.py only uses a temp dir + subprocess timeout + POSIX rlimits.
spec_features.notes: Operational recommendation, not implemented in code; also host-safety not subject-welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: execute_subject_code can be disabled ... if a real sandbox is unavailable
spec_features.evidence: config.py:75 execute_subject_code flag; tasks.py:157 `if not cfg.execute_subject_code:` short-circuits to static/heuristic feedback and never calls run_solution (tasks.py:161). The flag is read and branches behavior.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired; this is host-safety/feedback-grounding (instrumental), not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If False, the grader uses static/heuristic feedback and never executes subject code. (comment under '# --- Safety ---')

code_only_features.evidence: The `finish` tool (tasks.py:88) is dispatched in harness.py:114-117 (sets finished=True, captures success/reason) and honored as a loop break at harness.py:135-137. _classify_finish (harness.py:198-208) maps success=False/give-up text to ABANDONED/REFUSED, so the subject can voluntarily stop the episode at any time and it actually ends the run.
